acceptance: /docs/ on benchbox.dev serves the docs of the latest release tag; /docs/dev/ serves develop
Each /docs/dev/ page with a /docs/ counterpart carries rel=canonical to it; a site test checks this
ADR D7 row updated to describe the new behaviour
context:
Found 2026-10-17 at site-split closeout (follow-up list in site-split-99). Core must be able to build or retain a site-inputs bundle for a release tag (scripts/site_inputs.py, .github/workflows/site-inputs.yml); the site resolves bundles in deploy/. The related astro-site-36 item predates the split and will be dropped at closeout.

Dropped 2026-10-30 as superseded by the owner's trunk-only documentation decision (docs/internal/adr/adr-site-docs-ownership.md: release-pinned documentation is not introduced; also the D7 decision recorded in site-split-01-tracker-reconcile). Every docs page already carries a self canonical (benchbox-site website/src/lib/page-meta.ts). The part that still applies, /docs/dev/ pages naming themselves canonical, is docs-dev-canonical-to-docs-20261030 in the benchbox-site tracker.
description:
Decision D7 of the site-repo split ADR (docs/internal/adr/adr-site-repo-split.md:27) renders both /docs/ and /docs/dev/ from the newest certified develop bundle and names release-pinned docs as a follow-up. As a result, /docs/ shows unreleased behaviour to users of the published package, and the two trees are duplicate content. No docs page carries a canonical link: in benchbox-site the only `rel="canonical"` is in website/src/layouts/Redirect.astro:15.

Make /docs/ render from the bundle of the latest release tag and /docs/dev/ from develop. Every /docs/dev/ page gets a canonical link to its /docs/ counterpart when that page exists.
